authority: Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation (OCABR), Home Improvement Contractor Program (HIC registration); Construction Supervisor Licence (CSL) is issued separately by the Board of Building Regulations and Standards under the Division of Occupational Licensure
notes: Massachusetts has two regimes. (1) HIC is a registration for residential home-improvement contractors. The MA Contractor Hub is operated by OCABR, and its home page lists only HIC services: search, complaint, Guaranty Fund and arbitration. The old HIC lookup at services.oca.state.ma.us/hic/licenseelist.aspx returned HTTP 503. (2) CSL is a licence for individuals who supervise permitted building work. Neither the CSL lookup URL nor any CSL bulk file was established. The DOL eLIPSE search (occupationallicensingandpermitting.mass.gov) license-type list included plumbing, gas fitting and sheet metal, but no Construction Supervisor type was seen in it. Plumbers, gas fitters and sheet-metal workers are licensed at state level through DOL eLIPSE. mass.gov pages returned 403 to every automated fetch, so no program page text was read. No bulk download was found.

authority: Board of Registration of Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons (Division of Occupational Licensure)
notes: The request route comes only from a search-result snippet of a 2018 DPL 'request for public information' form. The snippet described a Public Record Unit at 1000 Washington St, 617-727-0809, with 'Real Estate Sales and Brokers' databases sent on CD-ROM for a $30 fee. mass.gov returns 403 to automated fetches, so the form was not read and may be stale. The live per-licence lookup is DOL eLIPSE: https://occupationallicensingandpermitting.mass.gov/madol/s/license-search-page (fetched; it offers Real Estate Salesperson, Broker, Corporation and LLC types). The legacy lookup elicensing21.mass.gov/CitizenAccess also resolves (200).

authority: Dept. of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA), Bureau of Construction Codes, Licensing Section (Residential Builder and Maintenance & Alteration Contractor licences under Article 24 of PA 299 of 1980)
notes: The state licence is residential only: Residential Builder, Maintenance & Alteration Contractor, Builder Company, M&A Company, Residential Builder Salesperson and Branch Office. The same BCC Licensing Section also licenses electrical, mechanical, plumbing, boiler and elevator trades. Residential builders moved to Accela on 2019-08-26. No public bulk list for BCC licences was found; the free Accela FOIA reports on the professional-licensing page do not cover builders. For bulk data, try LARA FOIA (https://www.michigan.gov/lara/foia-request) or lara-bcc-licensing@michigan.gov, 517-241-9316.

authority: LARA, Bureau of Professional Licensing (Real Estate Brokers & Salespersons)
file_format: Excel, generated on demand (the page says some reports come out as PDF)
notes: Linked from https://www.michigan.gov/lara/bureau-list/bpl/license-lists-and-reports as 'FOIA-Real Estate Brokers/Salesperson List'. The report link resolved (HTTP 200) but I did not generate the report. The page says the report covers active licences only and includes name, profession name, profession type, status, expiration date, address, issue date, specialties and email. It does not mention a licence number. Related reports on the same page: Real Estate Active Employees (reportID 32068) and Real Estate Employer Info of Active Licenses (reportID 32088).

authority: Minnesota Department of Labor and Industry (DLI), Construction Codes and Licensing Division
file_format: csv (the all-divisions file is a zip: https://secure.doli.state.mn.us/ccld/data/MNDLILicRegCertExport.zip, 11.1 MB)
approx_rows: approx 50,000–60,000 (estimated from 12.2 MB size; includes non-active statuses)
notes: Linked from https://www.dli.mn.gov/license-and-registration-lookup. I read the header row: Bus_Pers, License_Type, License_Subtype, Name, DBA_Name, Addr1, Addr2, City, St, Zip, Phone_No, Email_Address, Lic_Number, Status, Orig_Date, Exp_Date, Enforcement_Action, Renewal_in_Progress. There is no county or qualifier field. Current licences carry status 'Issued'. The state licence is residential building contractor/remodeler; License_Subtype also covers types such as Manufactured Home Installer. Separate CSVs exist for electrical, plumbing, mechanical contractor bond, boiler, elevator, high-pressure piping, water conditioning and construction contractor registration, all at the same /ccld/data/ path. No commercial general-contractor licence was identified.

authority: Minnesota Department of Commerce (Licensing)
notes: Commerce's 'Look Up A License Holder' page (https://mn.gov/commerce/licensing/license-lookup/) sends 'Real Estate, Agent/Agency/Broker' to pulseportal.com. That is a vendor-hosted lookup Commerce links to, not a mn.gov domain. mn.gov sits behind a bot wall, so I read it in a browser. No bulk file was found. A search snippet suggested a standing public-records request route, but that is not established. Contact: licensing.commerce@state.mn.us, 651-539-1599.

authority: Mississippi State Board of Contractors (MSBOC)
notes: MSBOC issues both commercial licences ($400 fee; CPA-reviewed net worth of $50k for a major classification or $20k for a specialty) and residential licences ($50 fee), per msboc.us/contractors/licenses. The search host search.msboc.us returned a Cloudflare error (1033 / HTTP 530) when checked, so the lookup could not be confirmed live. No downloadable roster was found on msboc.us. Contact: info@msboc.us, 601-354-6161.

authority: Mississippi Real Estate Commission (MREC)
notes: The lookup resolves (HTTP 200). A company search is at mrecPublicCompanySearch.aspx. No bulk roster was found. Contact: 601-321-6970.

authority: No state general-contractor licence. The Division of Professional Registration licenses electrical contractors statewide ('Electrical Contractors' board).
notes: The no-GC finding for general contractors rests on the absence of any GC board in the DPR board list. The MOPro 'Downloadable Listings – Active License Only' page loads its board dropdown from a server call, and the returned board list includes 'Electrical Contractors'. No general-contractor, plumbing or HVAC board appears in that list. The page is a Salesforce app whose dropdown would not render in automation, so I did not generate a file and could not see its format or fields.

authority: Missouri Real Estate Commission (Division of Professional Registration)
notes: 'Real Estate' is one of the boards in the Downloadable Listings dropdown (active licences only), confirmed from the page's own server response. Format and fields were not established because the dropdown did not render in automation. pr.mo.gov/realestate.asp links to it as 'DOWNLOADABLE LISTINGS'. Per-licence search: https://mopro.mo.gov/license/s/license-search.

authority: Montana Department of Labor & Industry, Business Standards Division – Construction Contractor License (CCL) program
notes: HB 239 (2025) turned the old Construction Contractor Registration into a licence effective 2026-01-01; registrations active on 2025-12-31 converted automatically. The board page (boards.bsd.dli.mt.gov/construction-contractor/) says 'All construction contractors with employees must register'. The paid route is a 'Licensee Mailing List' record request inside the ebiz POL portal. The realty board page says lists cost money and exclude email and phone; I found no separate statement for contractors. Free per-licence lookup: https://ebizws.mt.gov/PUBLICPORTAL/searchform?mylist=licenses.

authority: Montana Board of Realty Regulation (Dept. of Labor & Industry, Business Standards Division)
notes: From the board's license-information page: a mailing list of licensees by licence type can be downloaded and purchased through the Business Standards Division. The same page says there are no email or phone numbers in the list and there is a cost. app.mt.gov/download/ now redirects to the POL portal. The 'address' field is inferred from the term 'mailing list', not from a field list. Free lookup: https://ebizws.mt.gov/PUBLICPORTAL/searchform?mylist=licenses.

authority: Nebraska Department of Labor – Contractor Registration (Nebraska Contractor Registration Act)
notes: This is a registration, not a competency licence. The Act requires all contractors and subcontractors, including general contractors, to register, and the search page itself says registration 'does not ensure quality of work'. The search filters by DBA or corporation name, city, zip, phone, registration number, state, county and NAICS service code. Contractors whose workers' comp certificate lapses are removed from the list. No bulk file was found. State trade licensing (for example electrical) was not researched. Contact: NDOL.ContractorRegistration@nebraska.gov.

authority: Nebraska Real Estate Commission
notes: The lookup is linked from nrec.nebraska.gov as 'Search for Licensee or Business' and resolves (HTTP 200). No roster or download was found on the commission site. Contact: realestate.commission@nebraska.gov, 402-471-2004.

authority: Nevada State Contractors Board (NSCB)
file_format: HTML listing (free, active only); the paid list comes as Excel or PDF
cadence: daily (results show 'Information Current as of' a same-day timestamp)
terms: free for the active HTML directory; fee for other lists ($100 up to 500 records, $200 above)
notes: NSCB licenses all contractors: A General Engineering, B General Building, and C-1 to C-42 specialties. Its 'Active Directory of Licensed Contractors' can be filtered by county (or All) and primary classification (or All). I ran one small test query; results show name, address, phone, licence number, classifications, expiry, monetary limit and status. It is served as HTML, not a file. Inactive, revoked, surrendered and cancelled lists must be bought via the Contractor List Request form (https://www.nvcontractorsboard.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Contractor-List-Request.pdf, read, revised 12/2021). That list includes business name, licence number, status, expiration date, classification/limitation, monetary limit, mailing address and phone. The classification list is shown in the listing dropdown; no separate code-list URL was fetched.

authority: Nevada Real Estate Division (Department of Business and Industry)
notes: Index page: https://red.nv.gov/Content/Administration/Active_Licensee_Lists/ ('updates lists of active licensees... on a monthly basis'). Separate files exist for NRED-ACTIVE-BROKERS.xlsx, NRED-ACTIVE-BROKER-SALESPERSONS.xlsx, property managers, business brokers and others, all at the same path. Files were confirmed by HEAD only and not opened, so the columns are not established. Lookup: https://red.prod.secure.nv.gov/Lookup/LicenseLookup.aspx.

authority: No state general-contractor licence. Trades are licensed by the Office of Professional Licensure and Certification (OPLC): Electricians' Board and the plumbing/mechanical board.
cadence: daily (roster filename and 'As of' date change daily)
notes: The no-GC finding and the board names come from third-party guides seen in search results, not from an OPLC page. They say NH has no statewide GC licence and that electricians, plumbers and fuel-gas fitters are licensed via OPLC. Treat as unverified at an official source. The linked file is OPLC's 'Updated Roster of all other Licensees', covering every non-real-estate board, so trades must be filtered out of it. The index page (https://www.oplc.nh.gov/list-oplc-licensees-and-their-license-types) was read in a browser. The filename is dated, so the URL changes with each update; resolve it from the index page. The file itself was not opened.

authority: New Hampshire Real Estate Commission (Office of Professional Licensure and Certification)
notes: Listed on https://www.oplc.nh.gov/list-oplc-licensees-and-their-license-types as 'Updated Roster of Real Estate Licensees... (As of 09/28/2026)'. OPLC says the list 'is updated on a regular basis but is not real-time'. The filename is dated, so re-resolve it from the index page. The file was not opened, so columns are not established. oplc.nh.gov returns 403 to plain fetches; I read it in a browser.

authority: Division of Consumer Affairs, Office of Consumer Protection (Home Improvement Contractor registration); DCA Bureau of Homeowner Protection (new home builder registration)
cadence: real-time (the system describes itself as real-time)
terms: free (the download page says phone numbers are no longer included)
notes: NJ has no state GC licence. Home-improvement contractors register as 'Home Improvement Business Contr'; there is also a 'Home Elevation Business Contr' type. The bulk verification site takes a profession filter; I ran one test search limited to one city. Results show name, licence number, profession, licence type, status, city and state, with a 'Download List' option for the whole result set, including expired registrations. I did not click Download List. Other trade boards on the same system include Electrical Contractors, Master Plumbers and HVACR. New-home builders register separately with DCA: search at https://serviceportal.dca.nj.gov/ultra-bhp-home/bhp-home-builder-search/ (200). The DCA Data Hub 'NJ Homebuilders List' item points to https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/publications/pdf_nhw/brlist.pdf, which returns 404; the item was last modified 2024-06-05. njconsumeraffairs.gov/requestlist is behind Incapsula and could not be read.

authority: New Jersey Real Estate Commission (Department of Banking and Insurance)
cadence: daily (search reflects changes the next day)
notes: Instructions page: https://www.nj.gov/dobi/division_rec/licensing/online_Instructions/licSearch.html. Active and inactive licensees can be searched by name, licence reference number, licence type or status. No bulk file was found. A Socrata catalog query found no licensee dataset for NJ or for any other state in this batch. Contact: relic@dobi.nj.gov, 609-292-7272.
